card.name: Hooping
card.tagline: manipulation of and artistic movement or dancing with a hoop (or hoops)
card.profile: Hooping (also called hula hooping or hoop dance) is the manipulation of and artistic movement or dancing with a hoop (or hoops). Hoops can be made of metal, wood, or plastic. Hooping combines technical moves and tricks with freestyle or technical dancing. Hooping can be practiced to or performed with music. In contrast to the classic toy hula hoop, modern hoopers use heavier and larger diameter hoops, and frequently rotate the hoop around parts of the body other than the waist, including the hips, chest, neck, shoulders, thighs, knees, arms, hands, thumbs, feet, and toes.
card.insight: In March 2013, the largest hula hoop workout (407 participants) was achieved at Ravenscraig Regional Sports Facility in Scotland by North Lanarkshire Leisure and Powerhoop Fitness.
sources: Source: Hooping on Wikipedia, CC BY-SA 4.0. Read: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hooping

lessons.title: Beginner Hoop Tricks

parts.note: welcomes viewers and introduces beginner hoop tricks
teaches duck out of hula hoop

steps.name: Isolation Hooping
steps.description: Keep hand underneath and move in a circle while keeping the hoop in the same position.

steps.name: The Vortex
steps.description: Spin hoop, wrap it, bring it above you, and guide it around your body.

steps.name: Duck Out
steps.description: Duck your head through the hoop as it hits your back.

steps.name: Basketball Isolation
steps.description: Isolation with hand on top of the hoop making a steering wheel motion.

steps.name: Lasso
steps.description: Spin the hoop above your head and bring it down in a circle in front of you.

common_mistakes: putting hand on top instead of underneath during isolation
lessons.teacher_style: The teacher is friendly, encouraging, and breaks down tricks step-by-step in an outdoor garden setting. She uses descriptive imagery like 'driving' and 'basketball' to explain hand positions.
lessons.distinctive_method: uses common everyday analogies like driving a car and playing basketball to explain hand coordination.
what_works: clear visual demonstrations of hand placements
breaking down tricky maneuvers into slower steps
what_hinders: some transitions between steps lack detailed explanations

evidence.observation: teacher demonstrates isolation hooping holding the hoop with one hand
teacher demonstrates the vortex trick moving the hoop around her body

lessons.title: Hoop Isolations Tutorial - Pulsing, Pushing & Sliding

parts.note: Teacher introduces the lesson and mentions viewer requests.
Pulsing isolation breakdown with two hands and one hand.
Push isolation breakdown, emphasizing body movement and angles.
Combining all three isolation styles in a continuous flow.
Summary of the importance of weight and balance in isolations.

steps.name: Pulsing Isolation
steps.description: Rocking the hoop side to side along its upper arc using a pencil grip.

steps.name: Push Isolation
steps.description: Pushing the hoop through the air with a soft grip, incorporating body lunges.

steps.name: Sliding Isolation
steps.description: Drawing a line then a circle, whipping the hoop out and back to the body.

images: Like a bubble floating through the air
Hand acts like a ledge or a shelf
common_mistakes: Letting the circle fall under during a sliding isolation
Standing still while pushing the hoop, which reduces energy
Pushing the hoop too far from the body during a slide
lessons.teacher_style: Deanne Love uses a highly encouraging and descriptive teaching style, focusing on the sensory experience of hooping. She breaks down complex isolations into manageable components like 'pulsing' and 'sliding' while emphasizing body engagement.
lessons.distinctive_method: The teacher uses a 'pencil grip' and 'brush stroke' terminology to bridge the gap between fine motor hand control and large-scale hoop movement.
what_works: Clear visual metaphors help conceptualize the movement path.
The teacher demonstrates the moves from multiple angles to show body integration.
what_hinders: The lack of a specific counting scheme might make it harder for some to time the transitions.

evidence.observation: Teacher explains the difference between basic circular isolations and the pulsing variation.
Demonstration of pulsing isolation with two hands, moving the hoop in a semi-circle.
One-handed pulsing isolation showing the hand rolling over the back of the hoop.
evidence.cannot_infer: exact finger placement on the back of the hoop

evidence.observation: Push isolation demonstrated with a side lunge and the hoop moving horizontally.
Sliding isolation shown at the front, side, and back of the body.
